claims.text: LLMs utilizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation can still generate unsupported or contradictory claims relative to retrieved content.
RAGTruth is a corpus constructed for analyzing word-level hallucinations across various domains and tasks in standard RAG frameworks.
RAGTruth contains nearly 18,000 naturally generated RAG responses from diverse LLMs.
Responses in RAGTruth feature manual annotations at both case and word levels evaluating hallucination intensity.
Finetuning a relatively small LLM on RAGTruth achieves hallucination detection performance competitive with prompt-based approaches using GPT-4.

evidence.description: Despite the integration of RAG, LLMs may still present unsupported or contradictory claims to the retrieved contents.
This paper presents RAGTruth, a corpus tailored for analyzing word-level hallucinations in various domains and tasks within the standard RAG frameworks for LLM applications.
RAGTruth comprises nearly 18,000 naturally generated responses from diverse LLMs using RAG.
These responses have undergone meticulous manual annotations at both the individual cases and word levels, incorporating evaluations of hallucination intensity.

using a high-quality dataset such as RAGTruth, it is possible to finetune a relatively small LLM and achieve a competitive level of performance in hallucination detection when compared to the existing prompt-based approaches using state-of-the-art large language models such as GPT-4.

limitations.text: LLMs integrated with retrieval-augmented generation may still produce outputs that are unsupported by or contradictory to the retrieved contents.
